title: Current viewer authorization revision profile v1
description: The rule that decides, at the moment of display or delivery, whether one viewer may see one projection of one subject. docs/privacy/PRIVACY_CONTRACT.md is the normative owner. SR-015 records that the repository stated the requirement — display and delivery always recheck current blocks, privacy and membership — without naming what is rechecked, against which revision, or what happens when a check is racing a change. This file names all three. It has no persistence owner and deliberately no cached decision: a stored authorization result is the defect SR-015 describes, so the only durable state is the revision of each input aggregate, each of which already has its own owner.

inputs.description: Every aggregate a decision reads. Each names its persistence owner and the revision column that makes a stale read detectable. A decision that read fewer than all of these is not a partial decision; it is a wrong one.

surfaces.description: Every surface that must evaluate the profile. A surface absent from this list is a surface that publishes without checking, which is how a block becomes advisory.

revision_source.description: The column that changes when the input changes. Where an aggregate has no revision column the state column itself is named, and that is recorded rather than papered over: a state comparison detects a change and cannot order two of them.

effect.description: deny-hard is absolute and no other input can restore it. deny-unless-authorized is the default for a private subject. widen only ever adds visibility to a subject who has not denied it.

recheck_point.description: read-time is a check performed as the response is built. delivery-time is a check performed as an already-created inbox item is handed to a viewer, which is the one D-084 and the notification contract need: a notification created while a viewer was authorized must not be delivered after they were blocked. snapshot-time is the single exception and applies only to a sealed ranking generation, whose content_hash covers no handle and no authorization state precisely so that a later block changes what renders without changing what was sealed.

order.description: Deny inputs are evaluated before widen inputs, so a widen can never overtake a deny by arriving first. The order is fixed rather than left to a query planner because two orders produce two answers for a viewer who is simultaneously a friend and blocked.

cache_policy.description: No authorization result is cached anywhere, including in a request-scoped memo that outlives the statement that produced it. A projection may be cached only when it is identical for every viewer, which is true of a sealed generation's figures and of nothing else.

race_resolution.description: The decision reads every input inside the same read-committed statement and compares the revisions it read against the revisions present when the response is emitted. A change under it fails the request rather than serving the earlier answer, because the participant who pressed block is entitled to assume it took effect and a retry costs one request.

failure_mode.description: An input that cannot be read is a deny. An authorization system whose outage widens access has the wrong default.
